title: Officer rushes into pond to save 5-year-old boy with autism who wandered away from home
text:
ST. PAUL, Minn. (KARE) - Dramatic video shows a Minnesota police officer rush into a pond to save a 5-year-old boy with autism struggling in the water.

St. Paul Police Officer Adisak Sae Ma rescued a 5-year-old boy with autism from a pond Monday. Police say they launched a drone to help find the boy after good Samaritans spotted him and called for help.

“When I got there, he was treading water,” Sae Ma said. “I called out to him, but then, he moved farther away from me to the deep end of the water. I took off my gear, and I just went in there.”

Sae Ma was able to safely scoop the 5-year-old boy into his arms and wade over to the shore as seen in drone footage released by police. The boy was taken to the hospital to be checked out. Police say his family told them he had wandered away from their home without them knowing.

“I feel like everyone in my uniform would do the same thing,” said Sae Ma of the rescue, adding he was scared he wouldn’t make it in time. “I had a call like that before, but it didn’t end that way. A lot of times, we show up, and it’s too late.”

He’s convinced St. Paul’s Docked Drone Program was the difference this time.

St. Paul is one of several Minnesota cities that have installed the automated rooftop drones this year, deploying them as first responders on certain emergency calls. The three drones have already logged at least 1,500 flights since the end of May.

“We can get there much faster than a lot of the officers,” said Police Sgt. Matt St. Sauver, who helps lead the department’s Real Time Information Center. “In this case, the drone got to the scene two minutes before officers. We were able to tell them exactly where the child was, what the child was doing. We could see that the child was kind of going deeper into the pond.”

The large volume of drone flights, along with the company behind the technology, Skydio, has drawn concern and pushback from some community members. Members of the St. Paul City Council say they are looking for more data on the drones and the risks versus benefits they carry.

However, in the case of Monday’s rescue, police say their value as a tool is pretty clear.

“You couldn’t ask for a better situation or a better solution,” St. Sauver said. “If we know what we’re going into, the officers can prepare and deal with that situation with a better handling of knowing the information that they can have.”
